about: Home's painting as an empty plate plus furniture layers: the hand-traced source. Painting px of art/scenery/home/background.png (1536x1024), traced by eye on 2-3x zooms with a 10px grid (2026-09-13). layers.py reads this and writes art/scenery/home/layers.json. `body`: polygons hugging the item's silhouette ~2px outside (solid: alpha 1 inside, the difference matte decides only the edge band); `foliage`: polygons where the whole inside is difference-matted (leaves, fringes); `mask`: the generous hole sent to the edit API, taking in the contact shadow; `footprint`: where the item meets the floor (feet of legs, base of a cushion); `extent`: the widest part dropped to the floor when it overhangs the footprint (a tabletop), used for depth and clearance; `height`: floor to the top of the item itself, px; `anchors`: proposals.

inventory.why: the low table with its books, lantern, plant, small stack and mug stands in the middle of the rug; she walks all round it, and close behind it is where the hand-traced map failed
the tasselled floor cushion in front of the table: she passes behind it (between it and the table's left leg is too tight, but along its left and right) and in front of it
the quilted green floor cushion in front of the table, the same

the green armchair with its star pillow and two throws: against the bookcase, so she is only ever in front of it or beside it, but it is where she sits (armchair.sit), and the chair's front edge is the floor's edge there
the round side stool with its books and a small plant, beside the armchair; she stands beside it and in front of it, and it carries a place anchor

the writing desk under the window, with its cabinet, lamp, books, open book, mug and the potted plant on its left end: against the wall, so only in front of or beside her, but it is where she writes and reads
the desk chair with the throw over its back, standing out from the desk: she can stand beside it with its back overlapping her

the railing and posts round the stair going down at the front, with the ivy on its first post: she is only ever behind it, and its posts and rail cross her feet when she stands at the floor's front edge

the stair up through the arch on the right: built into the wall and the arch; she can only stand in front of it, and cutting it would mean inventing the wall under it. Stays in the plate; its bottom step is a blocker for the floor

the low bookcase with the record player, its plants, pots and candle stack along the right wall: against the wall, she can only be in front of it, and cutting it would mean repainting the wall. Stays in the plate; its front is the floor's edge
the log basket and the poker bucket beside the stove: on the hearth corner against the walls, behind anywhere she can stand. Stays in the plate
the stove on its hearth: architecture (the brief keeps the fireplace in the plate); the hearth's edge bounds the floor
the ivy hanging off the left wall's outer corner and from the ceiling beams: outside the room's floor, never near her
the big rug and the runner: floor (the brief keeps them in the plate)
walls, the window, the bookcase over the armchair, pictures, the banner, the lamps on the walls: never in front of her

E.note: Not a floor hole: the lantern and the pool of its light on the tabletop, cut out of the table layer (lantern.py, called by plate.py). The hole is the tabletop (the table's extent raised by its height, inset 3px) within groundRadius of the lantern's base (a ground circle: page px across, times the iso slope down the page), less the other things on the table grown 2px, plus the lantern's body grown 2px. Its candidate is the unlit reference the lantern's light is measured against.

F.note: The fill under the lantern: its body grown 5px, less the other things grown 1px. A tight hole, so the generator continues the planks from the painting right beside it; E's candidate, repainting the whole pool, puts the plank joints elsewhere.

objects_note: Things Lumi picks up, cut out of the layer they stand on (lantern.py). `body`: the silhouette traced ~2px outside, as a layer's body; `base`: the centre of its base where it meets the surface, painting px as painted; `grip`: where a hand takes it (the top of the ring on its finial; the painted lantern has no bail handle); `drawnHeight`: the height it is drawn at in the room, px (Chanté, 2026-09-13: ~40, a third of her 120); `at`: the anchor it starts at; `cluster`: its inpaint cluster.
floor_note: The floor her feet may stand on, ignoring furniture: the walk test's first hand-traced floor (since retired), pushed out where the plate shows more floor (up to the hearth, the wall base right of the stool, the stair's bottom step) and already inset from walls, rug-free edges and the floor's front edge by her cloak's reach. Walkable = this minus every footprint (extent where given) and blocker grown by her clearance.
